F-T04-1.explanation: ELI5: the test harness writes all four messages (hello, ack, list-tools, call-tool) to the server in one go and slams the door (closes stdin) right after. Real servers that do any async work to answer the last message sometimes lose the race between finishing that work and the door slam, so their answer never comes back. A version that waits for each answer before asking the next question never loses this race. Why it matters: this was misdiagnosed twice before as a missing handshake step and as a tap defect. Neither is true -- driver.py already sends the full initialize/notifications-initialized/tools-list/tools-call sequence, and the exact same drop happens with the tap completely removed (direct Popen, batched write). The tap is exonerated. The actual fix belongs in the test harness's I/O pattern (write-then-close is unsafe against async servers), not in glassport itself, so this is scored P2 (harness limitation) rather than a product defect.
F-T04-1.provenance: manual diagnostic sessions + 6 driver.run_session trials against pip mcp-server-time/mcp-server-fetch 2026.7.10 in venv-rec; fixtures/mcp-server-time-diagnosis.jsonl, fixtures/mcp-server-fetch-diagnosis.jsonl (captured, scrubbed real tap logs)
F-T04-1.title: Real MCP-server stdio correlation failures are a batch-write/stdin-close race, not a handshake gap or tap defect

F-T04-2.explanation: T04 tested tap resilience to abrupt termination: (1) SIGKILL on server mid-session - partial requests logged, all JSONL lines parse; (2) stdin close + SIGKILL on client - 3 complete log lines preserved; (3) NEW client-kill scenario per dispatch - client process killed mid-call, JSONL integrity maintained. All three cases pass: tap exits cleanly without log corruption.
F-T04-2.title: T04 abrupt shutdown resilience (all three cases)

F-T05-001-sse-named-preserved.explanation: ELI5: The HTTP tap correctly records SSE event names (e.g., 'message') in the session log. Why: Named events enable detection of protocol-level streaming frames, not just JSON-RPC payloads. All 4 responses (tools/list + 3 tools/call) preserved metadata in both clean and abrupt lifecycle tests.
F-T05-001-sse-named-preserved.provenance: HTTP tap test (T05) confirmed sse_meta with event names in JSONL
F-T05-001-sse-named-preserved.title: Named SSE metadata preserved end-to-end

F-T05-002-correlation-perfect.explanation: ELI5: All JSON-RPC tool calls get matched with their responses in the log, regardless of HTTP framing. Why: This ensures the tap's relay path doesn't lose messages. All 3 tool/call attempts per run matched their responses; abrupt shutdown still logged all complete events before termination.
F-T05-002-correlation-perfect.provenance: Synthetic HTTP server × 3 framings × 2 lifecycle tests, correlate() verified
F-T05-002-correlation-perfect.title: Call correlation 100% across all framings

F-T05-003-sse-metadata-not-in-direct-jso.explanation: ELI5: When the server doesn't use SSE framing, the HTTP tap doesn't add fake SSE metadata to the log. Why: The metadata is only meaningful when present in the wire protocol. Direct JSON is correctly logged without sse_meta; SSE framings preserve whatever metadata arrived.
F-T05-003-sse-metadata-not-in-direct-jso.provenance: Grep count of sse_meta field in direct_json vs sse_named logs
F-T05-003-sse-metadata-not-in-direct-jso.title: Direct JSON responses do not include sse_meta (expected)

F-T05-004-abrupt-shutdown-safe.explanation: ELI5: Killing the tap mid-session doesn't corrupt the log file - all preceding events are valid JSON lines. Why: JSONL is append-only and line-oriented; truncating the file after a complete event keeps it valid. Abrupt shutdown recorded all 4 responses before termination; no partial JSON.
F-T05-004-abrupt-shutdown-safe.provenance: Killed tap server after 4 complete SSE events; JSONL remains parseable
F-T05-004-abrupt-shutdown-safe.title: Tap survives abrupt shutdown without log corruption

F-T05-005-fastmcp-sse-named.explanation: ELI5: Real MCP server sends SSE responses with named events (event: message, id: N), and all calls are logged and correlated. Why: Named SSE framing is the production format; verifying it end-to-end with real SDK ensures tap handles real-world protocol. Both clean and abrupt termination preserved all sse_meta (5 entries = initialize + tools/list + 3 tools/call responses).
F-T05-005-fastmcp-sse-named.provenance: Official mcp Python SDK (v1.28.1) FastMCP server with streamable-http transport, tested through HTTP tap
F-T05-005-fastmcp-sse-named.title: FastMCP real server uses SSE named framing with metadata preservation

F-T07-0.explanation: ELI5: two of the five durability cases (C1: does logging trouble stop the relay; C5: does a long, slow-paced run hold up) had been reported earlier with numbers that don't add up -- a '100-call, 600+ second' test that supposedly finished in 0.18 seconds. Those two are now re-run for real: C1 with an actual chmod'd directory and a captured subprocess PID, and C5 as a genuine ~10-minute paced session with memory samples taken every 25 calls. Why it matters: the earlier numbers were physically impossible (100 calls at any real pace can't finish in 0.18s), so they could not be trusted as evidence of durability. The corrected C1/C5 entries carry wall-clock, PID, and RSS data a reviewer can independently sanity-check against the timestamps in durability-checkpoint.json. C2-C4 are left as the original driver-based runs but now explicitly labeled as such (return code + response counts only, no PID/wall-clock instrumentation) so nobody mistakes them for the same evidence tier as C1/C5.
F-T07-0.provenance: b1_result.json + b2_result.json (scratch rec/); durability-checkpoint.json b2_checkpoints array; durability-0610.json C1/C5 entries
F-T07-0.title: Durability C1/C5 re-run with real evidence (PID, wall-clock, RSS); C2-C4 flagged as driver-only evidence

F-T08-1.explanation: Running `glassport tui` in a non-terminal environment (Docker, CI, agent subprocess) raises `_curses.error: cbreak() returned ERR`. The README does not mention this requirement in the Quick Start section 6, though it is implicit to anyone familiar with curses. ELI5: The TUI needs a real terminal to control cursor and colors. Why it matters: Users in CI/Docker environments or following along programmatically will encounter an unexplained error. Recommendation: Add a note in Quick Start § 6 like '(requires a terminal; run on localhost)'.
F-T08-1.title: TUI requires terminal; fails in non-PTY environments

F-T08-2.explanation: The 'Query the history' section introduces `glassport serve` as an MCP server that reads session logs, but does not mention that logs must be in the default ~/.glassport/sessions or that `--log-dir` can override it. A user with logs in a custom directory will discover this by trial or by reading the help text. ELI5: serve assumes you store logs in one place; if you don't, you won't know why the agent can't see them. Why it matters: Low friction for most users (the default location is fine), but reduces discoverability of log-dir customization. Recommendation: Add a brief note in 'Query the history' or a link to the serve args in help.
F-T08-2.provenance: README section 'Query the history'; tested with synthetic serve call
F-T08-2.title: glassport serve uses hardcoded ~/.glassport/sessions; --log-dir not mentioned in quickstart
